notes:
The noun form of ⟦{割|わ}り{込|こ}む→割り込む：06973_warikomu⟧ (to cut in, to push in). In everyday life, it most commonly refers to cutting in line or merging aggressively in traffic — both considered rude in Japanese culture. In computing, it refers to hardware or software interrupts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {割|わ}り{込|こ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to cut in line
- {割|わ}り{込|こ}み⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧: no cutting in line
- ⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧な{割|わ}り{込|こ}み: reckless cutting in (traffic)
- {割|わ}り{込|こ}み⟦{処理|しょり}→処理：03251_shori⟧: interrupt processing (computing)
- {割|わ}り{込|こ}み⟦{信号|しんごう}→信号：03258_shingou⟧: interrupt signal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{横入|よこい}り→横入り：25288_yokoiri⟧: cutting in line — more colloquial and used almost exclusively for queues, not traffic or computing
- ⟦{割|わ}り{込|こ}む→割り込む：06973_warikomu⟧: to cut in; to squeeze in — the verb form, covering both physical cutting in and interrupting
